title: Audition voices before making every clip
statement: Choose a narration voice from auditioned, timed takes of the real script, judged by what is heard and checked word for word, not by catalogue descriptions or requested settings.
example: An audition on one 86-word scene caught a model reading its style instruction aloud, and that model was ruled out.
detail: The handover for a narrated opening offered three candidate voices from catalogue adjectives alone, with no listening comparison, and asked that the audition start with the canonical first passage, which tests place-setting, warmth, tragic reversal, name pronunciation, pacing and dramatic restraint in a small sample, and that the voice be selected on its actual output. The audition that followed made ten takes of the 86-word first scene across two models and three voices. It caught one model reading its style instruction aloud, a fault a later re-transcription found in all four of that model's takes, and a model that leaks direction into speech was not trusted across the eight clips.
against: The final choice was not made by ear: the model judges split among the voices, and "With no decisive human preference recorded, the handover's first candidate wins the tie." (g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/DECISION.md, line 30); no person had yet listened when the voice was chosen (same file, lines 3 and 32). Pace readings can be confounded by what a clip holds: in an earlier audition the extra length of one model's takes was a spoken instruction, not slow delivery (g9/narration/auditions/2026-10-06-scene1/DECISION.md, line 41).
